text: dsh-continuechat 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的会话续接插件。它在宿主侧注册 `/continue` 命令，并在被中断的助手回复下方添加继续操作。用户可以在手动停止、请求失败或输出截断后重新排入续接提示，也可附加补充指令；插件观察会话事件来识别可续接的轮次，并通过浏览器命令接口调用宿主命令。适合希望从中断位置接着完成 DSH 对话的用户。代码未显示需要额外 API 密钥或外部服务。

dsh-continuechat resumes interrupted DSH web conversations. It provides `/continue` and a Continue button below interrupted replies. After a stop, failed request, or truncated output, users can queue a continuation, optionally with extra instructions. Session events identify resumable turns.
想从刚才被我停止的 DSH 回复接着写。
模型请求失败后，能不能继续刚才没完成的对话？
让 DSH 在输出被截断后从断点续写。
dsh-continuechat 的功能「命令续接」：通过 `/continue [补充指令]` 请求继续空闲会话中被中断的工作。命令根据记录的中断原因生成续接提示，并将其排入 agent；若会话仍在运行则返回错误。
dsh-continuechat 的功能「回复下方继续按钮」：当最近一轮以可续接原因结束时，在对应助手消息的操作栏显示 Continue 按钮。点击后通过浏览器远程命令接口执行宿主 `/continue`，并显示执行失败状态。

dsh-continuechat README · dsh-continuechat：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Manually resume an interrupted DeepSeek Harness conversation.

When a turn ends early — stopped by hand, cut short by a failed model request, or truncated by the output-token limit — the harness leaves nothing behind but a "stopped" marker. This plugin adds the missing step: a `/continue` command and a **Continue** action in the action row under the interrupted reply itself, so the run picks up exactly where it stopped instead of restarting.

dsh-continuechat README · What it solves：| Situation | Without the plugin | With the plugin |
|---|---|---|
| You hit stop by accident | Retype "continue" yourself | Click **Continue** |
| A network or provider failure aborted the turn | Restate the context before the model resumes | The plugin hands the recorded failure to the model and resumes |
| The reply was cut off by the token limit | The harness says *send "continue"* — with no entry point | One click or one command continues the answer |

dsh-continuechat README · Command：```
/continue
/continue also fix the remaining three files
```

Text after the command name is appended to the continuation prompt as an "Additional instruction from the user" line.

The command's outcome (`已请求继续对话（中断原因：手动停止）。`) is rendered by the harness command plane; it never becomes a model message.

dsh-continuechat README · Button：On the turn that was cut short, a **Continue** action appears in the action row under the closing assistant message — the same row that carries copy / thumbs-up / thumbs-down / branch:

dsh-continuechat README · Button：- **It only appears on a real interruption.** Turns that completed, were blocked, or merely closed a fork show nothing, so the button never shows up under a conversation that ended normally.
- Only the assistant message that closes that turn carries it; every other message renders nothing and takes no space.
- It disappears again once the agent is running.
- Clicking it is exactly one `/continue` execution.
- A failed attempt keeps a short error line next to the action (hover for the full text).

dsh-continuechat README · Button：The decision comes from the session's durable event window: the newest `turn/end` must have a resumable reason *and* that turn must carry a **persistent** assistant message. A turn that was interrupted **before producing any assistant output** (a request that failed outright, a process that died before streaming) therefore has nowhere to host the button — use the `/continue` command there.
dsh-continuechat README · Command menu：Type `/` and pick `continue` ("Continue the interrupted conversation from where it stopped"). Arrow keys plus Enter are enough — no draft typing required.
dsh-continuechat README · Interruption tracking (host half)：The plugin subscribes to the session log's `session/event` and tracks every turn end:

dsh-continuechat README · Interruption tracking (host half)：| `reason.kind` | Meaning | Resumable |
|---|---|---|
| `aborted` | Run cancelled. `reason.reason.kind` refines it: `user` stopped by hand, `parent` stopped by a parent operation, `hook` stopped by a harness hook, `disposed` session torn down | ✅ |
| `error` | Model request failed (network, auth, server) | ✅ |
| `max-tokens` | Reply truncated by the output-token limit (not a context-window overflow) | ✅ |
| `interrupted` | Turn closed by crash recovery after the host process was interrupted | ✅ |
| `completed` | Finished normally | ❌ |
| `blocked` | Step refused by `agent/pre-step` before entering | ❌ |
| `forked` | Fork seed closing an inherited prefix (the start of a new session) | ❌ |
dsh-continuechat README · Interruption tracking (host half)：Any later `user/message` clears the record — either the user took over, or the plugin already resumed the run.

dsh-continuechat README · The continuation prompt：`/continue` does not send a bare "continue". It queues a structured user message:

```
<continue-conversation>
The previous turn ended early: the run was stopped by hand.
Continue the interrupted work in this same session, from exactly where it stopped:
- Do not restart the task, re-summarize, or repeat output and work that is already visible above.

dsh-continuechat README · The continuation prompt：The first line is rewritten per reason (stopped by hand / request failed / reply cut off / crash recovery), and the harness-recorded failure text is attached so the model knows *why* the turn ended — which is what decides between continuing to write and re-checking an interrupted tool call first.

dsh-continuechat README · Why the answer is a separate message：After you press **Continue**, DSH opens a new turn for the model to write on, and the plugin then retires that turn's trigger prompt from the transcript — so you no longer see the prompt, and the interrupted reply is followed directly by the new text.
section: Why the answer is a separate message

text: dsh-continuechat README · Why the answer is a separate message：The retirement is a `system/message` replacement, and the log makes such an event *step-scoped*: its `turn`/`step` must name the step that is open as it lands, and both coordinates must be positive (`dsh-session-format-v3-to-v4/lib/index.js`, `assertV4SystemMessageFields` plus the relationship replay). A turn that has already ended names no open step, so the replacement cannot be written there. It rides the step that produced the model's answer to the prompt — or, for a turn that produced none, the next step that opens.
section: Why the answer is a separate message

text: dsh-continuechat README · Why the answer is a separate message：The new text **cannot be merged into the original message**. That is an architectural constraint of the DSH session log, not an implementation shortcut:
section: Why the answer is a separate message

text:
dsh-continuechat README · Why the answer is a separate message：- The log is event-sourced: a committed assistant message cannot be edited, only shadowed by a surface `replace`.
- A `replace` must list every shadowed node in `sourceEventSeqs` (`dsh-session/lib/index.js:327`), while `assistant/message` is explicitly forbidden from carrying that field (`:313`, it embeds its provider stream). The two rules conflict, so no assistant event can perform a replacement.
- Shadowing the whole range with a `system/message` instead would also shadow the `tool/call` / `tool/result` pairs inside it, breaking the model history so the next request fails.
section: Why the answer is a separate message

text:
dsh-continuechat README · Why the answer is a separate message：The provider side has no assistant prefill either (`dsh-llm-deepseek` carries only anthropic-beta flags), so the model cannot literally continue the previous assistant message — it must generate a new one.

The result: **no stray "continue" prompt, but still a separate new answer.**
section: Why the answer is a separate message

text: dsh-continuechat README · Message shape：The continuation message is built by hand as `{ id, role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'text', text }], source: { kind: 'continue-chat' } }` and frozen:

dsh-continuechat README · Message shape：- **The `id` is mandatory.** `Agent.inbox` deduplicates pending messages by `message.id` (a duplicate throws `already pending`) and never mints one, so the plugin generates it with `randomUUID()` from `node:crypto`.
- **`source.kind` is `continue-chat`.** Chat classifies a `user/message` by its source kind: `user` would render the prompt as a human bubble, while any other kind renders it as an injected-context node — and a context node whose content is plain text stays out of the visible node set. Never use `'plugin'` either: that is only the legacy format-v3 shape and format v4 rejects it when reading a log back.
- As a result the host half imports **nothing but `node:crypto`**: no `peerDependencies`, and therefore no exposure to the plugin version-compatibility gate.

dsh-continuechat README · The browser half：The client half does exactly two things:

1. Registers the `continue-chat` dictionaries (zh/en).
2. Registers one action in the `conversation.chat.assistant-actions` slot. That slot's owner prop is `messageId` and its entries render inside Chat's `MessageIconActions` — the very component that owns copy / rating / branch — so the button lands in that row by construction.

dsh-continuechat README · The browser half：Clicking it runs `ctx.remote.commands.execute(sessionId, '/continue', [])`, the same path a hand-typed `/continue` takes, so command lifecycle records, result rendering, and logging all stay identical.

dsh-continuechat README · The browser half：Whether a message belongs to an interrupted turn is answered by the session's own durable event window: `ctx.sessions.binding(sessionId).eventSource` is a plain `getSnapshot()`/`subscribe()` store, which the plugin reads through `React.useSyncExternalStore` — newest `turn/end` reason plus the `message.id` of that turn's last `assistant/message`. Snapshots are memoized per `revision`, so dozens of messages share one scan and the untouched rows never re-render.

dsh-continuechat README · Install：```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add <absolute path to this directory>
```

The `dsh.bundle.patch` field points at `cordis.patch.yml`, which inserts the `continue-chat` row into the profile; `dsh.client.platform = "web"` makes the host serve `lib/client.js` as a browser bundle.

Remove it with:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-continuechat
```

dsh-continuechat README · What it deliberately does not do：- **It never continues on its own.** Every trigger is human: a command, the button, or your own typing. For automatic continuation use the `goal` tool.
- **It never shows the button under a normally finished conversation.** The decision comes straight from the session log's `turn/end` reason, not from a guess about which turn is last.
- **It never merges the new answer into the previous message.** That is impossible in this architecture (see above); the continuation is always a new assistant message, and the plugin only retires its own trigger prompt.
- **It never cuts in while the agent runs.** `/continue` against a running agent reports an error instead; stop the turn first.
- **It never rewrites history.** A continuation is one new user message appended to the log.
- **It never retires a prompt outside an open step.** The replacement is written from inside the step that answers the prompt, or from the next step that opens when a turn ends without an answer. That is the only position the log accepts, and it is why the retirement is not part of the `turn/end` handling.

text:
dsh-continuechat README · Development：- `lib/index.js` — host half: interruption tracking plus the `/continue` command.
- `lib/client.js` — browser half: a hand-written `window.__ModuleLoader__` bundle (no build step).
- `test/host.test.mjs` — drives the host half through a tiny fake cordis context.
- `test/client.test.mjs` — drives the browser bundle through a tiny fake React.
- `tools/inspect-session.mjs` — decompresses a session log (many concatenated zstd frames) and lists the `/continue` triggers, retirement events, and turn boundaries, for checking the surface bookkeeping: `node tools/inspect-session.mjs <session dir>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`.
- `tools/verify-retirement-coordinates.mjs` — runs the harness's own released-V4 validator over the three candidate coordinates, proving that only a replacement inside an open step is accepted: `node tools/verify-retirement-coordinates.mjs <app root>`.
